headline: Gratitude Remembers. Advent Waits.
headline_sub: What Advent Is, and the Battle in the Waiting
seo_title: What Is Advent? Waiting for Jesus Before Christmas
seo_description: What is Advent? The four weeks before Christmas are a season of waiting. A devotional for men on what the wait reveals and how to enter Advent this year.
og_image_alt: Gratitude Remembers. Advent Waits.: Yesterday we looked back at what God did. Today we start waiting on what He said He would do. TheWrkShop.

scriptures.text: I wait for the LORD, my whole being waits, and in his word I put my hope. I wait for the Lord more than watchmen wait for the morning, more than watchmen wait for the morning.

blocks.text: Today the season turns.
GRATITUDE REMEMBERS WHAT GOD HAS DONE. ADVENT WAITS FOR WHAT GOD HAS SAID HE WILL DO.
So what is Advent? It is the four weeks before Christmas when Christians wait and prepare for the coming of Jesus.

items: But before every arrival there is a wait.
And in the wait, there is a battle.

blocks.text: Most men are trained to work. Few are trained to wait.
Waiting feels like losing ground. So we fill it.
Today a lot of the country starts getting ready for Christmas with a shopping list. That’s not wrong. But it isn’t Advent.
The world gets ready for Christmas by gathering. Advent gets ready by watching.
A delay always asks a question: What does this mean?

items: “I’ll believe it when I see it.”

blocks.text: Those aren’t facts. They’re interpretations.
WHATEVER WE AGREE WITH IN THE WAITING IS WHAT WE BRING TO THE ARRIVAL.
Every person in the Christmas story had to wait. Every one of them had to decide what God’s interruption meant.

items: A priest who had stopped expecting an answer.
A young woman whose yes would cost her reputation.
A good man about to make a reasonable, quiet, wrong decision.

blocks.text: Four times, before God said anything else, He said the same thing: “Do not be afraid.”
God spoke to the fear before He spoke the news.
Take a moment and name what you’re waiting on God for this year.
Then ask: What have I been telling myself this wait means?
Gratitude remembers. Advent waits.

Father, thank You for what You have already done. As this season turns, teach me to wait on what You have said You will do. Show me what I have been telling myself the waiting means, and give me the courage to agree with You instead. In Jesus’ name, Amen.
Gratitude looks back. Advent leans forward.
What we agree with in the waiting is what we bring to the arrival.
Christmas was decided upstream.
